18732012
CLAIMS
WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. A rotor assembly, comprising: a propeller; a motor including a stator and a rotator rotatable with respect to the stator, and configured to drive the propeller to rotate through the rotator; and a connection assembly arranged between the propeller and the motor, and including a locking member and an elastic member, the elastic member being configured to provide a force onto the locking member in response to the propeller being locked to the motor by the locking member, to maintain a locking state of the locking member.
2. The rotor assembly of claim 1, wherein the rotator includes a rotating shaft, the rotating shaft passing through an accommodation space defined by the locking member and an accommodation space defined by the elastic member.
3. The rotor assembly of claim 2, wherein the connection assembly further includes a restrainer, and the rotating shaft passes through an accommodation space defined by the restrainer.
4. The rotor assembly of claim 3, wherein the restrainer and the elastic member are coaxially arranged.
5. The rotor assembly of claim 3, wherein the restrainer or the elastic member includes a through hole for the rotating shaft to pass through.
6. The rotor assembly of claim 3, wherein the rotating shaft passes through the accommodation space defined by the elastic member, the accommodation space defined by the restrainer, and the accommodation space defined by the locking member, successively.
7. The rotor assembly of claim 1, wherein the rotator includes a housing and a rotating shaft, and the locking member is configured to rotate with respect to the housing of the rotator to lock the propeller to the motor.
8. The rotor assembly of claim 7, wherein the housing includes a connecting surface facing the propeller, the elastic member being in contact with the connecting surface.
9. The rotor assembly of claim 8, wherein the rotating shaft protrudes toward the propeller from the connecting surface by a predetermined distance.
10. The rotor assembly of claim 1, wherein the elastic member is configured to provide a longitudinal force onto the locking member in response to the propeller being locked to the motor by the locking member.
11. The rotor assembly of claim 1, wherein: the locking member includes a first locking unit; the propeller includes a second locking unit matching the first locking unit; and
the first locking unit is coupled to the second locking unit in response to the propeller being locked to the motor.
12. The rotor assembly of claim 1, further comprising: a first alignment marker provided at a rotating side of the rotor assembly during a locking process; a second alignment marker provided at a non-rotating side of the rotor assembly during the locking process, the first alignment marker and the second alignment marker being configured to algin along a radial direction of the propeller in response to the propeller being locked to the locking member.
13. An aerial vehicle comprising: one or more rotor assemblies each including: a propeller; a motor including a stator and a rotator rotatable with respect to the stator, and configured to drive the propeller to rotate through the rotator; and a connection assembly arranged between the propeller and the motor, and including a locking member and an elastic member, the elastic member being configured to provide a force onto the locking member in response to the propeller being locked to the motor by the locking member, to maintain a locking state of the locking member.
14. The aerial vehicle of claim 13, wherein the rotator includes a rotating shaft, the rotating shaft passing through an accommodation space defined by the locking member and an accommodation space defined by the elastic member.
15. The aerial vehicle of claim 14, wherein the connection assembly further includes a restrainer, and the restrainer or the elastic member includes a through hole for the rotating shaft to pass through.
16. The aerial vehicle of claim 14, wherein the connection assembly further includes a restrainer, and the rotating shaft passes through the accommodation space defined by the elastic member, an accommodation space defined by the restrainer, and the accommodation space defined by the locking member, successively.
17. The aerial vehicle of claim 13, wherein the rotator includes a housing and a rotating shaft, and the locking member is configured to rotate with respect to the housing of the rotator to lock the propeller to the motor.
18. The aerial vehicle of claim 13, wherein: the rotator includes a housing and a rotating shaft; the housing includes a connecting surface facing the propeller, the elastic member being in contact with the connecting surface; and the rotating shaft protrudes toward the propeller from the connecting surface by a predetermined distance.
19. The aerial vehicle of claim 13, wherein: the locking member includes a first locking unit; the propeller includes a second locking unit matching the first locking unit; and the first locking unit is coupled to the second locking unit in response to the propeller being locked to the motor.
20. The aerial vehicle of claim 13, wherein each of the one or more rotor assemblies further includes: a first alignment marker provided at a rotating side of the each of the one or more rotor assemblies during a locking process; a second alignment marker provided at a non-rotating side of the each of the one or more rotor assemblies during the locking process, the first alignment marker and the second alignment marker being configured to align along a radial direction of the propeller in response to the propeller being locked to the locking member.
